mechanism: Polyvalent cations chelate oral ciprofloxacin in the gut, forming insoluble complexes that reduce fluoroquinolone absorption and can cause antibiotic failure.

management.monitoring: Watch for lack of clinical response to the antibiotic course.
management.patient_counselling: Do not take the antacid, mineral supplement or dairy at the same time as ciprofloxacin.
management.timing: Take ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before, or at least 6 hours after, the cation-containing product.
management.exceptions: Does not apply to intravenous ciprofloxacin (no gut chelation).

evidence.excerpt: <verify — oral ciprofloxacin to be taken 2 h before or 6 h after cation-containing antacids/multivitamins/dairy>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Polyvalent cations reduce oral ciprofloxacin absorption; separate dosing by the labelled interval.

mechanism: Polyvalent cations chelate oral levofloxacin, reducing fluoroquinolone absorption and risking antibiotic failure.

management.monitoring: Watch for lack of clinical response to the antibiotic course.
management.patient_counselling: Keep the antacid/iron/calcium product away from the levofloxacin dose.
management.timing: Take levofloxacin at least 2 hours before, or at least 2 hours after, the cation-containing product (member-specific: shorter interval than ciprofloxacin/moxifloxacin).
management.exceptions: Does not apply to intravenous levofloxacin.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — administer levofloxacin at least 2 h before or 2 h after cation-containing products>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Polyvalent cations reduce oral levofloxacin absorption; the labelled separation interval is 2 hours either side.

mechanism: Polyvalent cations chelate oral moxifloxacin, reducing absorption; moxifloxacin requires a WIDER separation than ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin.

management.monitoring: Watch for lack of clinical response to the antibiotic course.
management.patient_counselling: Keep antacids/iron/calcium/zinc/sucralfate well away from the moxifloxacin dose.
management.timing: Take moxifloxacin at least 4 hours before, or at least 8 hours after, the cation-containing product (member-specific: wider than the fluoroquinolone default).
management.exceptions: Does not apply to intravenous moxifloxacin.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — moxifloxacin to be taken at least 4 h before or 8 h after cation-containing products>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Polyvalent cations reduce oral moxifloxacin absorption; the labelled separation is 4 h before / 8 h after, wider than other fluoroquinolones.

mechanism: Tetracyclines chelate polyvalent cations, forming poorly-absorbed complexes that lower doxycycline exposure and risk treatment failure.

management.monitoring: Watch for lack of clinical response to the antibiotic course.
management.patient_counselling: Separate doxycycline from antacids, iron, calcium, zinc and bismuth; a small amount of milk with food is a lesser concern than concurrent supplements.
management.timing: Separate doxycycline from cation-containing products by at least 2-3 hours (representative tetracycline member — other tetracyclines may differ).
management.exceptions: Chelation applies to oral tetracyclines only.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — absorption of tetracyclines reduced by antacids, iron and other polyvalent cations; separate administration>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Polyvalent cations reduce oral doxycycline absorption; separate administration.

mechanism: Calcium, iron and other polyvalent-cation binders bind levothyroxine in the gut and reduce its absorption, risking under-treatment (raised TSH).

management.monitoring: Recheck TSH if consistent separation cannot be maintained.
management.patient_counselling: Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach and separate it from calcium, iron and antacids.
management.timing: Separate levothyroxine from cation binders by at least 4 hours.
management.duration: For as long as both are taken.
management.exceptions: This binder rule is resolved by clock-spacing; the pH-modifier (PPI) interaction is a SEPARATE rule not solved by spacing.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — calcium/iron/antacids reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate by at least 4 h>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Oral cation binders reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate dosing by at least 4 hours.

mechanism: Sustained reduction of gastric acidity impairs dissolution and absorption of levothyroxine (esp. tablets), lowering levels and raising TSH; unlike binders, this is NOT overcome by clock-spacing.

management.prescriber_action: Recheck TSH after starting, stopping or changing acid-suppressant therapy; the levothyroxine dose may need adjustment. Do not stop either drug at the counter.
management.monitoring: TSH about 4-8 weeks after any change in acid-suppressant therapy.
management.patient_counselling: Take levothyroxine the same way every day; tell your prescriber if you start or stop indigestion/heartburn medicines.
management.duration: For as long as the acid suppressant is used.
management.exceptions: Clock-spacing does NOT overcome continuous PPI acid suppression — manage by consistent administration plus TSH review, not separation alone.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — agents that reduce gastric acidity may decrease levothyroxine absorption; monitor TSH>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Acid suppressants can reduce levothyroxine absorption; monitor TSH after changes rather than relying on dose separation.

mechanism: Oral bisphosphonate bioavailability is very low and is abolished by food, coffee, juice, mineral water and polyvalent cations taken at the same time.

management.patient_counselling: Take alendronate first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of PLAIN water only; wait at least 30 minutes before any food, drink, other medicine or supplement; remain upright (sitting or standing) during that time.
management.timing: At least 30 minutes before the first food, drink, medicine or cation of the day; plain water only.
management.exceptions: Product-specific to alendronate — do NOT copy the 30-minute/plain-water rule to other bisphosphonates or delayed-release formulations without checking their own label.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — take on arising for the day with plain water, at least 30 min before first food/beverage/medication, remain upright>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Alendronate must be taken on an empty stomach with plain water, at least 30 minutes before any food, drink, other medicine or cation, staying upright.

mechanism: Oral risedronate absorption is reduced by food and polyvalent cations; the correct administration differs between the immediate-release and delayed-release products.

management.patient_counselling: Immediate-release risedronate: take on an empty stomach with plain water, at least 30 minutes before the first food/drink/medicine, stay upright. Delayed-release risedronate: take immediately AFTER breakfast with at least 4 oz of plain water, stay upright — do not apply the empty-stomach rule.
management.timing: Immediate-release: >=30 minutes before first food/drink/medicine, plain water, upright. Delayed-release: immediately after breakfast per its own label.
management.exceptions: Formulation-specific: delayed-release risedronate is taken WITH food and must not be managed like the immediate-release tablet; separate calcium/iron/antacid supplements from either formulation.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — immediate-release taken >=30 min before first food; delayed-release taken immediately after breakfast>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Risedronate administration is formulation-specific: immediate-release before food on an empty stomach; delayed-release after breakfast.

mechanism: Oral ibandronate bioavailability is abolished by food and polyvalent cations; it requires a LONGER pre-food fast than alendronate/risedronate immediate-release.

management.patient_counselling: Take oral ibandronate first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with a full glass of plain water only; wait at least 60 minutes before any food, drink, other medicine or supplement; stay upright during that time.
management.timing: At least 60 minutes before the first food, drink, medicine or cation of the day; plain water only.
management.exceptions: Product-specific 60-minute interval — do not substitute alendronate's 30-minute rule.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — take with plain water at least 60 min before first food/drink/medication, remain upright>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Oral ibandronate must be taken on an empty stomach with plain water at least 60 minutes before any food, drink, medicine or cation.

mechanism: Raising gastric pH reduces atazanavir solubility and absorption, producing subtherapeutic levels with risk of virologic failure and resistance; magnitude depends on the booster and treatment history.

management.prescriber_action: Confirm the regimen with the HIV prescriber before supplying the acid suppressant: boosted atazanavir has PPI dose caps and separation requirements, and PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients. Do NOT stop antiretroviral therapy.
management.monitoring: HIV viral load if an acid suppressant is used.
management.patient_counselling: Do not start over-the-counter antacids, H2 blockers or PPIs without telling your HIV clinic; the dose and timing matter.
management.timing: Where permitted: give boosted atazanavir and the PPI at least 12 hours apart with the PPI dose capped; separate antacids/buffered products by at least 2 hours; H2-antagonist limits and separation per label.
management.exceptions: Severity and permissibility vary by booster (ritonavir/cobicistat) and by treatment-naive vs treatment-experienced status — split from unboosted atazanavir at promotion if needed.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — acid-reducing agents decrease atazanavir exposure; PPI dose/timing restrictions; not recommended in treatment-experienced patients>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Acid suppressants reduce atazanavir exposure; use is restricted by booster and treatment history with dose caps and separation requirements.

mechanism: PPIs cause sustained gastric pH elevation that substantially reduces rilpivirine absorption, risking loss of virologic response and resistance; the label lists PPIs as contraindicated with rilpivirine.

management.prescriber_action: PPIs are contraindicated with rilpivirine — do not supply the PPI alongside rilpivirine; contact the HIV prescriber for an alternative acid-reducing strategy. Do NOT stop antiretroviral therapy.
management.patient_counselling: Do not take proton-pump-inhibitor heartburn medicines (e.g. omeprazole, esomeprazole) while on rilpivirine.
management.exceptions: H2-antagonists may be used only with strict separation (e.g. taken >=12 h before or >=4 h after rilpivirine); antacids taken >=2 h before or >=4 h after rilpivirine — these are the timed alternatives, distinct from the contraindicated PPIs. Verify against current label.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — proton pump inhibitors are contraindicated with rilpivirine due to reduced rilpivirine exposure>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Proton pump inhibitors are contraindicated with rilpivirine; H2-antagonists and antacids are permitted only with strict dose separation.

mechanism: Erlotinib solubility is pH-dependent; acid suppression lowers erlotinib exposure and may reduce anti-tumour efficacy. Sustained PPI suppression is NOT overcome by dose separation.

management.prescriber_action: Avoid PPIs where possible; clarify the acid-reducing plan with oncology. Do NOT stop the tyrosine-kinase inhibitor at the counter.
management.patient_counselling: Tell your cancer team before using any antacid, H2 blocker or heartburn medicine.
management.timing: PPIs: avoid (spacing does not help). Antacids: separate by several hours. H2-antagonist: take erlotinib about 10 hours after and at least 2 hours before the H2 dose (per label).
management.exceptions: Spacing overcomes antacids but NOT continuous PPI suppression; member-specific timing.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — concomitant acid-reducing agents decrease erlotinib exposure; avoid PPIs; antacid/H2 timing guidance>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Acid suppressants reduce erlotinib exposure; avoid PPIs and apply labelled timing for antacids/H2-antagonists.

management_override.prescriber_action: Hepatic impairment independently raises erlotinib exposure and toxicity risk; oncology should factor this into the acid-suppressant decision and any dose review.

mechanism: Dasatinib solubility is pH-dependent; PPIs and H2-antagonists markedly reduce dasatinib exposure and may reduce efficacy. Spacing does not overcome sustained suppression.

management.prescriber_action: PPIs and H2-antagonists are not recommended with dasatinib; if acid reduction is needed, antacids may be used with separation. Clarify with oncology; do NOT stop the TKI at the counter.
management.patient_counselling: Do not use PPIs or H2 blockers with dasatinib without oncology advice; if an antacid is needed, keep it well apart from the dose.
management.timing: Antacids: give at least 2 hours before or at least 2 hours after dasatinib. Avoid concurrent PPI or H2-antagonist.
management.exceptions: Antacid separation is acceptable; PPI/H2 suppression is not solved by timing.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — avoid concomitant PPIs and H2-antagonists; antacids may be given >=2 h before or after dasatinib>
evidence.normalized_proposition: PPIs/H2-antagonists reduce dasatinib exposure and should be avoided; antacids are permitted only with 2-hour separation.

management_override.prescriber_action: Hepatic impairment affects dasatinib handling; oncology should factor this into the acid-suppressant decision and any dose review.

mechanism: Oral ketoconazole tablets require gastric acid to dissolve and be absorbed; reduced acidity lowers absorption and antifungal efficacy.

management.prescriber_action: If acid reduction is unavoidable, the ketoconazole tablet should be taken with an acidic beverage and the antifungal response reviewed; clarify with the prescriber. Do not stop specialist antifungal therapy at the counter.
management.monitoring: Watch for lack of antifungal response.
management.patient_counselling: If you must take an acid-reducing medicine, take ketoconazole tablets with an acidic drink (e.g. a non-diet cola) and keep antacids well separated.
management.timing: Antacids/H2: separate by at least 2 hours. PPIs cause sustained acid suppression not solved by spacing — clarify with prescriber.
management.exceptions: The acidic-beverage advice is product-specific to ketoconazole TABLETS and must NOT be generalised to other azoles or formulations.

evidence.excerpt: <verify — drugs that reduce gastric acidity impair ketoconazole absorption; take with acidic beverage when acid reducers required>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Acid suppressants reduce oral ketoconazole absorption; where unavoidable, take the tablet with an acidic beverage and separate antacids.

management_override.prescriber_action: Oral ketoconazole is hepatotoxic and hepatically cleared; in hepatic impairment the prescriber should reconsider the antifungal choice rather than simply adding an acidic drink.

mechanism: Itraconazole CAPSULE absorption requires an acidic gastric environment; acid suppression markedly reduces absorption and antifungal efficacy.

management.prescriber_action: If acid reduction is unavoidable, itraconazole capsules should be taken with food and an acidic beverage, and the response reviewed; clarify with the prescriber. Consider whether a formulation whose absorption is not acid-dependent is more appropriate. Do not stop specialist antifungal therapy at the counter.
management.monitoring: Watch for lack of antifungal response.
management.patient_counselling: Take itraconazole capsules with food and an acidic drink (e.g. a non-diet cola) if you need an acid-reducing medicine; keep antacids well separated.
management.timing: Antacids: separate by at least 1-2 hours. PPIs cause sustained suppression not solved by spacing — clarify with prescriber.
management.exceptions: Applies to the CAPSULE formulation only; do NOT apply the acidic-drink advice to itraconazole oral solution (separate rule).

evidence.excerpt: <verify — reduced gastric acidity decreases absorption of itraconazole capsules; take with food/acidic beverage>
evidence.normalized_proposition: Acid suppressants reduce itraconazole CAPSULE absorption; take with food and an acidic beverage and separate antacids.

management_override.prescriber_action: Itraconazole is hepatotoxic and hepatically cleared (and a negative inotrope); in hepatic impairment the prescriber should review antifungal appropriateness, not simply adjust administration.
